### Binary Classification Model

This was the code to deploy the fitted binary classification model (ran in Emma-Scratchwork.ipynb inside scratchwork folder). We pasted it here to show how the parameters and model state dict was saved and reloaded to predict on the test set.

```{python, eval = FALSE}
# save parameters
binary_parameters = {'state_dict': best_model.state_dict(),
                    'n_features': X_train_t.shape[1],
                    'hidden': int(best['hidden']),
                    'dropout': float(best['dropout']),
                    'class_names': [str(c) for c in class_names]}

torch.save(binary_parameters, "../../results/claims_binary_model.pt")

# load saved dict 
binary_parameters = torch.load("../../results/claims_binary_model.pt", map_location = "cpu", weights_only = True)

# reload model 
reload_model = TextNN(n_features = binary_parameters['n_features'],
                      hidden = binary_parameters['hidden'],
                      dropout =  binary_parameters['dropout'])

reload_model.load_state_dict(binary_parameters['state_dict'])
reload_model.eval()                             

# predict on test set 
test_pred_binary = predict_probs(reload_model, X_test_t)

pred_df = test_clean_claims_df[['.id']].copy()
pred_df['bclass.pred'] = np.array(binary_parameters['class_names'])[(test_pred_binary > 0.5).astype(int)]
pyreadr.write_rdata("../../results/binary-preds-emma.RData", pred_df, df_name = "pred_df")
#print(pred_df)
```

By saving the best model's state dict, which is a dictionary mapping each layer to its learned weights and bias tensors, we can apply these weights to the test data without having to access the training data or repeat the training. This also prevents testing an over-fitted model, so our test result reflects the model's best true performance.

### MULTI

This code reloads the fitted multiclass TF-IDF/SVM pipeline and applies it to the unlabeled test pages. The saved pipeline includes both the fitted vectorizer and classifier.

```{python, eval = FALSE}
from pathlib import Path
import pickle
import sys

import pyreadr

# Support knitting from either the repository root or the scripts directory.
ROOT = Path.cwd()
if not (ROOT / "data").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent

sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
from predict_multiclass import parse_html_text, read_rdata_frame

# Load the fitted pipeline and test data.
with (ROOT / "results" / "claims_multiclass_model.pkl").open("rb") as model_file:
    multiclass_model = pickle.load(model_file)

test = read_rdata_frame(ROOT / "data" / "claims-test.RData", "claims_test")
if ".id" not in test or "text_tmp" not in test:
    raise ValueError("Test data must contain .id and text_tmp columns")

# Apply the same HTML preprocessing used by the prediction script.
test_text = test["text_tmp"].fillna("").map(parse_html_text)

# Predict and save the multiclass output.
pred_df = test[[".id"]].copy()
pred_df["mclass.pred"] = multiclass_model.predict(test_text)

output_path = ROOT / "results" / "multiclass-preds.RData"
pyreadr.write_rdata(str(output_path), pred_df, df_name="pred_df")
print(f"Saved {len(pred_df)} predictions to {output_path}")
```

The saved pipeline contains both the TF-IDF vectorizer and the fitted linear SVM. Reloading the pipeline applies the same learned vocabulary and term weights to the test pages before assigning each page one of the five multiclass labels; the model is not refit on the test data.
